Title: Solidatus glossary
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/additional-resources/solidatus-glossary
Content: A Data Map is an explorable visualisation of lineage and metadata that can stitch lineage together across multiple atomic and composite models.

Data Maps are integrated in Data Domains and are automatically generated when Lineage models are published to a Data Domain.

Data Maps offer the ability to summarise stages and entities in a lineage flow visually according to high-level business categories, taxonomies, and structures. This enhanced visual capability makes physical data items easy for everyone in an organisation to discover and understand through terminology that is meaningful across the business.

See also Data Domain
Title: Data Assets in domains
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/the-user-interface/data-domains-ui/data-assets-in-domains
Content: Blue connection lines: Indicate that connected entities are the same Data Asset across different models
Asset entity boxes: Data Assets appear as standard entities with grey headers in Data Maps
Asset side panel: When an asset is selected, the side panel shows consolidated Asset information

Cross-model lineage flows between assets in multiple models are automatically displayed when Data Assets are published to a domain.=

Blue lines in Data Maps are automatically generated when models containing the same Data Asset are published to a domain, enabling you to track cross-model lineage visually.

Title: Understand Data Maps
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-2026.2/data-domains/data-maps/understand-data-maps
Content: Data Maps are automatically generated when you publish Lineage models to a Data Domain. They serve as the primary visualization tool for exploring the data lineage landscape of a domain.

Use Data Maps when:

Visualizing end-to-end data flows that span multiple systems or models
Presenting technical lineage in business-friendly groupings
Building enterprise-wide data blueprints that are easy to navigate
Showing data context using organizational structures (systems, departments, processes)

Title: Explore a Data Map
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/data-domains/data-maps/explore-data-maps
Content: Data Assets in Data Maps appear the same as non-Data Asset entities: as boxes with a grey header.

Blue transitions show that two items are the same Data Asset

Blue, two-way transitions in a Data Map indicate that two connected items are the same Data Asset.

Blue transitions connect assets that exist in multiple models published to a domain, and they represent cross-model lineage connections. They are generated automatically by when you publish models that contain the same Data Asset to a domain.

You can also find out if something is a Data Asset by looking at the side panel that opens when you select it in the Data Map.

For Data Assets, the side panel has an Asset information section showing asset properties.

Logos and icons for Technology and Type asset properties are also displayed if values for these properties have been entered in the underlying models.

You can also see a Data Asset’s lineage in the Sources/Targets tab in the side panel.
Title: Data Map interface
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/the-user-interface/data-domains-ui/data-maps-interface
Content: The expanded Data Map views tile gives you access to all views that have been created in the Data Domain.

Search for a Data Map view by name.
Click the name of a Data Map view to open it.
You can delete a Data Map view from the three-dots menu.

Only Owners of a domain can create and delete Data Map views.
